    VLM4RSDet: Collaborative Optimization with Vision-Language Model for
               Enhancing Remote Sensing Object Detection

                       Shuohao Shi*                         Qiang Fang*, †                         Xin Xu*, †
             shishuohao23@nudt.edu.cn                   qiangfang@nudt.edu.cn                xinxu@nudt.edu.cn



                           Abstract

Closed-set object detection in remote sensing imagery
has made significant progress, but achieving high detec-
tion accuracy remains challenging. Vision-Language Mod-
els (VLMs), which possess rich prior knowledge, offer a
promising solution to this challenge. However, most exist-
ing VLMs are designed for open-vocabulary tasks and ex-
hibit inherent limitations when directly applied to closed-
set scenarios, such as notable accuracy degradation and
                                                                   Figure 1. The overview of VLM4RSDet. In the training stage,
high deployment costs. To address these issues, we propose
                                                                   we simultaneously optimize both the conventional object detection

any additional deployment overhead. Furthermore, we in-

Figure 2. The overall structure of VLM4RSDet. In the training stage, the model is optimized with a composite loss function that integrates
the conventional object detection losses (Lcls and Lreg ) with the language modeling loss Lllm . This optimization is performed collabo-
ratively, leveraging a series of shared multi-scale features Pi . In addition, we propose a Global-Local Cross Attention (GLCA, detailed
in Section 3.2) and a Learnable Hierarchical Prediction Strategy (LHPS, detailed in Section 3.3) to enhance the feature perception ability
and prediction output accuracy of vision-language model, respectively. In the inference stage, we only retain the standard object detection
architecture (as shown in the red dashed area), which will not bring additional overhead to model deployment.

Effectiveness of Each Proposed Module. The ablation                                       In this paper, we propose VLM4RSDet, a remote sensing
study of each module is shown in Table 6, New Struc-                                      object detection method that integrates the conventional ob-
ture refers to the collaborative optimization of conventional                             ject detectors with a vision-language model (VLM) through
object detection model and vision-language model during                                   collaborative training. This approach addresses two key
the training stage. It can be found that the New Struc-                                   limitations: the low accuracy of conventional object detec-
ture can improve the detection accuracy mAP0.5:0.95 by                                    tion models and the high deployment overhead of VLMs.
2.8%. On this basis, GLCA and LHPS can further improve                                    Furthermore, we introduce a Global-Local Cross Attention
mAP0.5:0.95 by 1.3% and 1.7%, respectively. If all three                                  module and a Learnable Hierarchical Prediction Strategy,
modules are employed simultaneously, the detection accu-                                  tailored for enhancing vision-language model in detecting
racy can be significantly improved by 5.7%.                                               densely distributed objects within remote sensing images.
Performance of Different Values of α. In the training                                     Extensive experiments demonstrate that VLM4RSDet sig-
stage, we introduce a weighting parameter α to balance the                                nificantly improves detection accuracy while maintaining
losses from conventional object detection model and vision-                               high efficiency, achieving state-of-the-art performance on
language model, as defined in (5). To further determine the                               multiple remote sensing object detection datasets.
best value of α, we conduct an ablation study. From Ta-                                   Limitations and Future Work. Our proposed collabo-
ble 7, it can be found that when α is set to 0.05, the model                              rative training method has effectively improved the accu-
achieves the highest detection accuracy.                                                  racy of conventional object detectors but remains confined
